title: I was doing (past continuous)
subtitle: was/were + -ing
summary: Use was/were + -ing to say what somebody was in the middle of doing at a time in the past.

lesson.heading: Paul at 4 o'clock and now
lesson.text: It is 6 o'clock now. Paul is at home and **he is watching** television. At 4 o'clock he **wasn't** at home. He **was** at the sports club. **He was swimming** in the pool. **He wasn't watching** television.

examples.text: At 4 o'clock he **was swimming** in the pool.

lesson.heading: In the middle of doing something
lesson.text: Paul started swimming at 3.30 and finished at 4.15. So at 4 o'clock **he was swimming**. He was in the middle of his swim. **I was doing something** = I started it before that time and I finished it after that time.

lesson.heading: Positive and negative
lesson.note: Spelling: live -> liv**ing**, run -> ru**nning**, lie -> **lying**.

lesson.heading: Questions
lesson.note: With a question word, put it first: *What **were** you **doing**?*

lesson.heading: Examples
lesson.text: We often use the past continuous to say what was happening at a time in the past, or to describe the background of a story.

examples.text: 'What did he say?' 'I don't know. **I wasn't listening**.'
**It was raining**, so we didn't go out.
I woke up early yesterday. It was a beautiful morning. The sun **was shining** and the birds **were singing**.

right.label: past: was/were + -ing
examples: **It wasn't raining** when we went out.

lesson.text: Say who or what you are talking about and then was or were: *she **was** reading*, not ~~she reading~~.

exercises.prompt: At 3 o'clock yesterday Jack and Kate were at the cinema. ___ a film.
exercises.explanation: they + were + -ing: They were watching a film.

exercises.prompt: At 3 o'clock Tracey was at the station. She ___ for a train.
exercises.explanation: She was in the middle of waiting, so: she was waiting.

exercises.prompt: Match each question with the right answer.

pairs.left: What were you doing at 2 o'clock?
Was it raining when you got up?
Why was Sue driving so fast?
Was Tim wearing a suit yesterday?

exercises.prompt: 'What did he say?' 'I don't know. I ___.'
exercises.explanation: The negative past continuous is wasn't/weren't + -ing: I wasn't listening.

exercises.prompt: Sarah played tennis from 10.15 to 11.45 yesterday. So at 10.45 ___ tennis.
exercises.explanation: 10.45 is in the middle of the game, so: she was playing.

exercises.prompt: Your friend has moved house a few times. Ask about 1999.

exercises.statement: In 2001 we were living in Canada.
exercises.explanation: Correct. was/were + -ing is the past continuous.

exercises.prompt: Sarah had breakfast from 7.10 to 7.25. So at 7.15 ___ breakfast.
exercises.explanation: At 7.15 the breakfast was not finished: she was having breakfast.

exercises.prompt: Is the sentence about now (present) or about a time in the past?

items.text: I was working at 10.30 last night.
It wasn't raining when we went out.
What were you doing at three o'clock?

exercises.statement: I woke up early. The sun was shine and the birds were singing.
exercises.explanation: The sun was shining and the birds were singing. After was/were the verb needs -ing.

exercises.prompt: Sue drove past you very fast. Ask why.
exercises.answer: Why was Sue driving so fast?

exercises.prompt: You saw Joe in the street. He had a shopping bag and he said 'I'm going shopping.' So ___ to the dentist.
exercises.explanation: Negative past continuous: he wasn't going to the dentist.
